result.summary: Validates the `inputs` option in the `sendall` RPC to reject duplicate outpoints. An `RPC_INVALID_PARAMETER` error is thrown immediately if the caller specifies the same UTXO more than once.
result.problem: When duplicate inputs are provided to `sendall`, the wallet counts their values multiple times and constructs a consensus-invalid transaction spending the same outpoint twice. The transaction fails mempool acceptance (`bad-txns-inputs-duplicate`), but is committed to the local wallet, locking the UTXOs and producing negative balance figures until the transaction is manually abandoned.
evidence: Description provides a regtest reproduction where passing a single 1 BTC UTXO twice to `sendall` returns `complete: true`, builds an un-broadcastable transaction with an output for ~2 BTC rejected for `bad-txns-inputs-duplicate`, empties `listunspent`, and leaves `getbalances` reporting `nonmempool: -1.0`.
result.changed_since_previous: Diff provided for the first time; implementation checks inputs with a `std::set<COutPoint>` in `src/wallet/rpc/spend.cpp` and adds a functional test case to `test/functional/wallet_sendall.py`.
result.card: Reject duplicate UTXO inputs passed to the sendall RPC. Previously, supplying duplicate inputs caused sendall to sum the UTXO value multiple times and generate consensus-invalid transactions (bad-txns-inputs-duplicate) that failed mempool acceptance and corrupted wallet balances until abandoned. The author demonstrates reproducible regtest behavior where a 1 BTC UTXO produced an un-broadcastable 2 BTC spend and a negative wallet balance.

risk.why: A flaw in wallet RPC transaction construction could reject valid inputs or improperly fail user transactions.
